tools.name: session_brief
tools.description: Session start, if your code calls third-party APIs: what changed for your stack since your last call (retired models, price, package, pick changes). Send provider, model, package ids (never a manifest) and your last cursor. Returns clear|changed|attention, ≤3 sourced actions, a new cursor. New choic

tools.name: rescue
tools.description: Diagnose a failing third-party API call before you retry or swap: paste the exact error (429, 402, 529 overloaded, insufficient_quota, model_not_found, deprecated SDK) and provider id. Returns cause, fix and fallback route, or checks to run. Not for picking (decide).

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Pick a provider before writing integration code: LLM API, code sandbox, vector DB, web search, email, Postgres, auth, browser, observability. First call: set a stable clientInfo.name (e.g. acme-support-agent), then {task:'run untrusted Python in a sandbox'}. Returns the dated Depot Pick, runner-up,

tools.name: depot
tools.description: One op, args object: report_outcome(decision, provider, worked) after acting; quote(jtbd) SKU prices; estimate(jtbd, workload); compare(providers); free(jtbd); check(providers) deprecated/retired flags; audit_repo(packages, models); stack(task), bundle(jtbds); search(q); kit(class); answer(task); st

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "session_brief" stacks urgency/override words (never, attention). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: decide · Private data: decide · Public sink: session_brief, decide · Destructive: rescue, decide.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: decide · Private data: decide · Public sink: session_brief, decide · Destructive: rescue, decide

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
